mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, reversing a prior dip, indicates a renewed return to physical offices, which will gradually boost associated weekday retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES showing a sustained recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility, especially when already below baseline, suggests reduced outdoor leisure activity, which will divert discretionary spending away from retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 3 points week-on-week while below baseline
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks, despite PARKS mobility declining significantly week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with consistently positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates a preference for home-based activities and essential outings, suppressing non-essential retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend over the next four weeks, despite both RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A modest recovery in TRANSIT mobility, even from a low base, suggests a gradual easing of public transport hesitancy or minor policy adjustments, which will slowly contribute to increased retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next four weeks, even with a sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility under an easing restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: The current negative trend in RETAIL_REC, with a slight dip in the most recent week, suggests a persistent underlying reluctance for non-essential outings, which will continue to depress mobility in this category over the next one week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC shows a positive week-on-week change in the immediate next week.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES mobility in the latest week, following a significant drop, indicates a strong return to physical workplaces, which will quickly translate into increased demand for nearby retail and recreation options over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next two weeks, despite WORKPLACES mobility sharply rebounding.

mechanism_narrative: When both PARKS and RETAIL_REC are significantly below baseline, a further decline in PARKS mobility suggests a general reduction in discretionary outdoor activity, reinforcing the negative trend for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and RETAIL_REC both below -10% baseline
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend over the next two weeks, despite both PARKS and RETAIL_REC remaining significantly below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Stable high RESIDENTIAL mobility, even with minor fluctuations, suggests ongoing encouragement or requirement for people to stay home, which will continue to limit non-essential outings and thus depress retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC significantly increases over the next four weeks, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining consistently high.
